methodology: Round 2 began with a formal project-value review of the 20 Round 1 gaps. Only G1-A/G2-A, G3-A and G4-A were authorized for targeted academic follow-up; G5-A was opportunistic and G10-A/G10-E were handed to Topic 03.

Manual terminology refinement and discovery preceded acquisition. Six clean PDFs passed a strict capability admission gate, bibliographic identity checks, PDF integrity checks, SHA-256 checks, extraction sanity checks and zero-duplicate comparison with the Round 1 corpus.

The frozen corpus contains one DIRECT_EMAIL_SUPPORT paper (C01), three TRANSFER_METHOD/ANNOTATION papers (A01-A03) and two TRANSFER_EVAL papers (B01-B02). Transfer evidence is not upgraded to direct email Topic evidence.

The Research Pipeline used a new isolated run. Search reconciliation used the frozen local manifest with provider attempts=[]; enrich was skipped by user execution boundary; download recorded 0 downloaded / 6 skipped_exists / 0 failed.

A run-local copy of previously working converter dependencies was verified, the runner performed a bounded retry, and attempt 2 converted 6/6 locally without modifying the installed Skill.

Six fresh high full-paper semantic workers ran with at most three concurrent processes and actual exit receipts. Five papers with material source ambiguity received separate focused xhigh adjudication; B02 did not require escalation. No max worker was used.

A deterministic adapter performed schema normalization, exact LF quote/raw-claim locator validation and only explicit xhigh finding repairs. All six final analyses validate against the installed paper schema with zero locator errors.

Cross-paper semantic reasoning was split into three independent xhigh sections (R2-A, R2-B, R2-C) and is assembled deterministically into this synthesis. Project/process findings with no paper evidence keep empty paper/evidence lists instead of fabricated citations.

D05 official-source acquisition failed once at DNS resolution and remains outside the corpus. The bounded R2-C discovery found no admitted modern task-matched business/work-email Topic-span benchmark; this is not a literature-absence claim.
No production mailbox data, design change, engineering benchmark implementation, deployment, or performance measurement occurred in this academic round.

taxonomy.finding: The four studies support distinct structural capabilities: multiple labels at one source location, overlapping mention boundaries, separated fragments belonging to one object, and shared words belonging to multiple instances. These capabilities do not establish one another or their joint use for msgloom Topics.
limitations: A01 describes entity-type and argument-subtype labels with incompletely specified combinations and decoding.
A03 explicitly supports simultaneous token labels but does not separately evaluate exact coincident span-label recovery.
A02 links fragments of an entity mention; repeated category labels alone do not supply object identity.
C01 demonstrates partial trigger sharing between instances of the same event type.
No study evaluates all these structures together for concrete work matters.
taxonomy.interpretation_notes: This distinction organizes the evidence. It does not approve a combined architecture. A msgloom Topic is a concrete work matter, not an entity type, propaganda technique, event type, or event instance.

taxonomy.finding: G1-A gains complementary gold-representation evidence. A02 contains discontinuous NER mentions with linked fragments. C01 directly establishes that an email event trigger can contain separated source words. Neither supplies gold identities for separated evidence belonging to one concrete work matter.
limitations: A02's discontinuous benchmarks are biomedical or clinical NER datasets.
C01's discontinuity applies to triggers; its argument spans remain continuous.
A01 links separate trigger and argument spans into events but defines individual candidate spans as contiguous.
These annotations do not establish authored-only email Topic prevalence or a within-email Topic prediction score.
taxonomy.interpretation_notes: C01 adds direct email support for a different semantic task. A02 adds a fragment-membership representation. Their combination strengthens the supporting evidence for G1-A while leaving its task-matched gold question open.

taxonomy.finding: Prediction evidence extends beyond representability but remains bounded. A02 reports an evaluation restricted to discontinuous entity mentions, although its numerical results are unavailable in the embedded conversion. C01 provides qualitative examples of BART recovering nearby shared triggers and reports difficulties at larger separation.
limitations: A02's full-dataset F1 values of 75.69, 83.80, and 82.12 pool flat, overlapping, and discontinuous mentions.
The evaluation of sentences containing discontinuous mentions is also distinct from discontinuous-only evaluation.
A02's general multi-fragment decoding procedure remains unresolved.
C01 supplies no shared-trigger subgroup denominator, distance threshold, or dedicated precision and recall.
Shared-trigger examples do not establish general discontinuous-trigger prediction accuracy.
taxonomy.interpretation_notes: A02 contributes structurally relevant NER prediction evidence with unavailable subset effect sizes. C01 contributes qualitative email-event prediction evidence. Neither contributes an email Topic prediction score.

taxonomy.finding: G2-A gains explicit methods for simultaneous source-location labels. A01 adds subtype classifiers to support multiple labels on a span. A03 trains a model with 23 binary technique decisions per token. Neither reports dedicated simultaneous-label accuracy.
limitations: A01 does not establish unrestricted simultaneous labels within a classifier family or every combination across families.
A01's standalone labeled-argument linking and complete output inventory remain unresolved.
A03's fixed technique inventory does not establish identities or assignments for concrete work matters.
A02 does not specify simultaneous multiple types for identical candidate boundaries.
C01's single BIOS label per word and specialized S tag do not establish a general multi-label token decoder.
taxonomy.interpretation_notes: The new contribution is explicit output capacity and training formulation. It is not measured recovery of simultaneous Topic memberships. A03's categorical news subjects are also not msgloom Topics.

recurring_patterns.finding: Observed structural prevalence remains separate from annotation capacity and prediction performance. A02 provides discontinuous-mention counts in its NER data. The other studies provide no numerical prevalence for the same-span or shared-trigger structures relevant here.
limitations: A02 reports 679 of 6,316 mentions in CADEC, 1,088 of 11,148 in ShARe13, and 1,656 of 19,070 in ShARe14 as discontinuous.
A02's count population is not clearly assigned to dataset splits, and overlapping and discontinuous counts are not disjoint categories.
A01 describes same-span labels as frequent without counts or label-combination distributions.
A03 reports neither coincident-label prevalence nor an overlap-specific gold subset.
C01's conditional mean of 3.05 repeated same-type events is not the prevalence of shared or discontinuous triggers.
recurring_patterns.interpretation_notes: NER counts, patient-level substance multiplicity, propaganda-positive paragraph counts, and repeated event counts cannot estimate authored-only email Topic overlap or discontinuity.

recurring_patterns.finding: The reported metrics evaluate different semantic objects and matching rules. They cannot be pooled into a structural assignment score or converted into expected msgloom accuracy.
limitations: A01's overall micro-F1 of 0.86 mixes overlap-tolerant trigger matching, exact span-only argument matching, and span-agnostic labeled-argument matching.
A01's trigger overlap tolerance does not measure recovery of overlapping entities or exact label co-location.
A02 uses strict typed-entity matching, but aggregate benchmark results do not isolate each mention structure.
A03 permits partial span credit and reports no simultaneous-label subset score.
C01's argument matching and aggregation remain unresolved. Its argument scores and sampled error-category shares are excluded from like-for-like cross-paper comparison.
recurring_patterns.interpretation_notes: Gold representability, model output capacity, observed prevalence, and evaluation success remain separate claims. None of these extraction metrics establishes exhaustive preservation of work-matter conditions or qualifiers.

recurring_patterns.finding: Annotation inputs and adjudication rules materially condition the evidence. A03's strongest GPT-4 setup uses human candidate annotations. C01 retains agreed annotation overlap and removes some disputed events or threads.
limitations: A03's explicitly index-corrected micro-F1 is 0.117 for Annotator and 0.670 for Consolidator, but these roles receive different human inputs.
GPT-4 editing permissions beyond candidate selection remain unresolved.
A candidate-coverage limit applies conditionally to selection-only operation; neither mechanical enforcement nor a numerical coverage ceiling is established.
First-occurrence index correction can select the wrong occurrence of repeated text.

reusable_mechanism_inventory.description: A01 retains Entity Type and Relation layers and adds three subtype-classifier families that permit multiple clinical labels associated with a span.
reusable_mechanism_inventory.generality: Limited clinical transfer-method evidence for same-span labels.
known_constraints: Unrestricted combinations within or across classifier families are not established.
Subtype-only argument linking through the Entity Type gate remains unspecified.
The complete implemented output inventory is unresolved.
Aggregate event-slot scores do not validate exact simultaneous-label recovery.

reusable_mechanism_inventory.name: Binary label vector per token
reusable_mechanism_inventory.description: A03 uses sigmoid outputs and binary cross-entropy to train 23 technique decisions per token, permitting several simultaneous positive labels.
reusable_mechanism_inventory.generality: Explicit multi-label output and training method for a fixed propaganda taxonomy.
known_constraints: No simultaneous-label subset accuracy or numerical gold-overlap prevalence is reported.
Token labels do not by themselves identify separated spans as one semantic object.
The fixed technique inventory does not establish a label system for concrete work matters.

reusable_mechanism_inventory.name: Shared-trigger encoding for event instances
reusable_mechanism_inventory.description: C01 uses a specialized BIOS sharing tag in BERT and filled event templates in BART. Gold examples allow the same trigger word to participate in separate same-type event instances.
reusable_mechanism_inventory.generality: Direct email-event representation with limited qualitative prediction support.
known_constraints: The sharing tag is not a general multi-label token output.
Same-type event-instance membership does not establish multiple Topic memberships.
Arguments are continuous and nonoverlapping within each event instance; this does not establish or exclude sharing across different instances.
Reliable prediction across separation distances is not demonstrated.

reusable_mechanism_inventory.name: Human-candidate-assisted annotation
reusable_mechanism_inventory.description: A03 supplies human span annotations to a selection-oriented GPT-4 consolidation procedure. Supplied spans and indices reduce dependence on generating source positions from scratch.
reusable_mechanism_inventory.generality: Annotation-workflow evidence, not autonomous Topic discovery or a measured cost-saving mechanism.
known_constraints: Boundary revision and relabeling permissions remain unresolved.
Candidate coverage is a conditional dependency under selection-only operation, not a measured recall ceiling.
First-occurrence index correction does not verify the intended occurrence of repeated text.
Agreement with consolidated gold does not establish exhaustive semantic coverage.

reusable_mechanism_inventory.name: Fixed reference-unit recall
reusable_mechanism_inventory.description: B02 separates writing reference-derived ACUs from judging each ACU's binary presence in candidate summaries. Reusing the written inventory fixes the denominator for later candidates. Raw recall is the fraction of those units judged present.
reusable_mechanism_inventory.generality: Transferable evaluation structure; validated here for human reference-summary matching.
known_constraints: The inventory represents reference-selected content.
ACUs have equal weight.
Matching agreement does not validate writing correctness or completeness.
The method does not by itself assess unsupported additions, automatic extraction, or Topic preservation.

reusable_mechanism_inventory.name: Training with uncovered reference content
reusable_mechanism_inventory.description: B01 predicts equivalence between reference and generated summary sentences using bidirectional NLI checks. Group matching uses consecutive sentences. Its uncovered loss trains on MixAndMatch summaries that combine uncovered reference sentences with matched generated sentences.
reusable_mechanism_inventory.generality: A summarization training mechanism with reference-conditioned coverage objectives.
known_constraints: NLI matches are predicted training signals, not human gold alignments.
One-direction entailment is not the full matching criterion.
The NLI component is absent at inference according to the embedded analysis.
The mechanism cannot explicitly recover information missing from its reference target.
It does not emit Topic labels, an omission inventory, or a coverage certificate.

reusable_mechanism_inventory.name: Separate whole-unit and within-unit omissions
reusable_mechanism_inventory.description: B01 distinguishes an entirely missing reference sentence from missing detail within a sentence. B02 demonstrates that a timing proposition can receive its own presence judgment. Together they support distinguishing whole-unit recovery from retention of a unit's details.
reusable_mechanism_inventory.generality: A transferable distinction for interpreting omission evidence.
known_constraints: The studies do not establish a common omission taxonomy or denominator.
B01's case categories are not known to be mutually exclusive.
C01's missing-value category does not systematically measure omissions within recovered argument text.
Qualifier scope and decision consequences remain unvalidated.

reusable_mechanism_inventory.name: Email context and event-specific argument structure
reusable_mechanism_inventory.description: C01 uses earlier messages as context and associates argument spans with event instances in the current email. Dates, times, confirmation values, and amendment context and revision roles provide concrete email annotation examples relevant to preservation.
reusable_mechanism_inventory.generality: Direct email support for event extraction and selected semantic roles.
known_constraints: Arguments are continuous and nonoverlapping within an event instance.
The taxonomy is selective and the full reported role inventory is unresolved.
Gold-trigger results remain separate from end-to-end results.
Context availability does not establish correct context use or complete history retention.
Event instances and roles are not concrete work-matter Topics.

reusable_mechanism_inventory.name: Evaluation target and length adjustment
reusable_mechanism_inventory.description: B01 separates reference recall, reference precision, and source faithfulness. B02 shows that human protocols can yield different system preferences and that normalized ACU adds a length-related penalty to raw reference-unit recall.
reusable_mechanism_inventory.generality: A measurement interpretation principle supported by summarization evaluations.
known_constraints: Protocol correlations do not establish the cause of annotator preferences.
Normalized ACU mixes coverage with a length preference.
Its exact normalization formula is not recoverable from the conversion.
A length penalty is not a direct measurement of semantic redundancy or precision.

reusable_mechanism_inventory.name: Specialized shared-trigger representation
reusable_mechanism_inventory.description: C01 permits separated trigger words and partial word sharing between same-type event instances. Its BERT baseline uses one BIOS label per word with an S tag for sharing, while BART generates event templates. The reported examples show that permitting a structure in gold does not ensure reliable recovery by a model.
reusable_mechanism_inventory.generality: Demonstrated for email event-trigger annotation and bounded qualitative prediction examples.
known_constraints: No unrestricted simultaneous different-label prediction is established.
No Topic segmentation or assignment evaluation is supplied.
Separation-distance effects lack a dedicated denominator, threshold, and subgroup score.

reusable_mechanism_inventory.name: Gold selection limits what recall can measure
reusable_mechanism_inventory.description: The annotation process retains agreed overlaps, removes disputed annotations, and limits the target taxonomy. Recovery of that gold can therefore measure extraction success only for retained content.
reusable_mechanism_inventory.generality: A measurement constraint illustrated directly by C01's annotation and evaluation design.
known_constraints: The size and semantic impact of excluded content are not established.
High annotation agreement does not establish exhaustive coverage.
Complete decision-bearing preservation requires a task-matched target that C01 does not provide.

reusable_mechanism_inventory.name: Conditional evaluation changes the question answered
reusable_mechanism_inventory.description: Supplying gold triggers conditions argument evaluation on correct event localization. Selecting erroneous outputs further changes the population to a failure subset. These results answer different questions from autonomous extraction performance and corpus-wide omission prevalence.
reusable_mechanism_inventory.generality: An evaluation distinction directly applicable to interpreting C01.
known_constraints: Gold-trigger results must remain separate from end-to-end results.
BART and GPT gold-trigger experiments additionally receive templates one at a time.
The error-analysis coding unit is unresolved.
Neither evaluation establishes Topic accuracy or complete qualifier preservation.

design_implications.finding: The four studies support distinct structural capabilities: multiple labels at one source location, overlapping mention boundaries, separated fragments belonging to one object, and shared words belonging to multiple instances. These capabilities do not establish one another or their joint use for msgloom Topics.
limitations: A01 describes entity-type and argument-subtype labels with incompletely specified combinations and decoding.
A03 explicitly supports simultaneous token labels but does not separately evaluate exact coincident span-label recovery.
A02 links fragments of an entity mention; repeated category labels alone do not supply object identity.
C01 demonstrates partial trigger sharing between instances of the same event type.
No study evaluates all these structures together for concrete work matters.
design_implications.interpretation_notes: This distinction organizes the evidence. It does not approve a combined architecture. A msgloom Topic is a concrete work matter, not an entity type, propaganda technique, event type, or event instance.

design_implications.finding: The reported metrics evaluate different semantic objects and matching rules. They cannot be pooled into a structural assignment score or converted into expected msgloom accuracy.
limitations: A01's overall micro-F1 of 0.86 mixes overlap-tolerant trigger matching, exact span-only argument matching, and span-agnostic labeled-argument matching.
A01's trigger overlap tolerance does not measure recovery of overlapping entities or exact label co-location.
A02 uses strict typed-entity matching, but aggregate benchmark results do not isolate each mention structure.
A03 permits partial span credit and reports no simultaneous-label subset score.
C01's argument matching and aggregation remain unresolved. Its argument scores and sampled error-category shares are excluded from like-for-like cross-paper comparison.
design_implications.interpretation_notes: Gold representability, model output capacity, observed prevalence, and evaluation success remain separate claims. None of these extraction metrics establishes exhaustive preservation of work-matter conditions or qualifiers.

design_implications.finding: No embedded study directly evaluates non-contiguous or simultaneous overlapping assignment to concrete work-matter Topics in email. G1-A and G2-A therefore remain open despite stronger supporting evidence.
limitations: A01 and A02 concern clinical extraction or NER.
A03 concerns propaganda techniques in Arabic news and tweets.
C01 concerns event and argument extraction in Enron.
C01's 2023 publication date does not make its underlying email corpus contemporary.
This conclusion concerns the embedded evidence, not the existence of evidence elsewhere in the literature.
design_implications.interpretation_notes: The section supports bounded academic strengthening only. It provides no architecture approval and authorizes no engineering experiment.

design_implications.finding: The section strengthens methods for evaluating omissions. It supplies no adjudicated rate of decision-bearing email scope loss caused by Topic segmentation. B01 and B02 provide summarization evaluation transfer. C01 provides direct email event-extraction support.
limitations: None evaluates segmentation or assignment of Topics defined as concrete work matters.
None isolates Topic segmentation as the cause of decision-bearing scope loss.
This conclusion concerns the embedded studies. It does not establish absence from the wider literature.
design_implications.interpretation_notes: G3-A remains open. Methodological strengthening does not supply the missing task-matched rate. This synthesis approves no architecture and authorizes no engineering experiment.

design_implications.finding: An explicit content inventory makes omissions measurable, but the inventory limits what the measurement can detect. B02 fixes a denominator of reference-derived Atomic Content Units. B01 identifies uncovered reference-summary sentences. C01 measures recovery of selected event arguments.
limitations: Important information omitted from a reference cannot enter reference-based recall.
C01 deliberately excludes content and prunes argument roles.
Neither reference faithfulness nor annotation agreement establishes inventory completeness.
design_implications.interpretation_notes: The shared contribution is a bounded denominator. The studies do not establish an exhaustive inventory of business-critical source information.

design_implications.finding: Coverage, source faithfulness, and reference precision are separate evaluation targets. B01 explicitly distinguishes them. B02 measures reference-fact recall without measuring unsupported additions. C01 separately reports missing, extra, incorrect, fabricated, and semantically correct nonmatching argument categories.
limitations: C01's error categories do not form a verified, consistent semantic partition.
B01's human scores are pairwise preferences, not absolute recall or accuracy rates.
B02's ACU matching protocol uses references without input documents.
design_implications.interpretation_notes: A source-supported statement absent from a reference can reduce reference precision without being a hallucination. A faithful output can still omit decision-bearing information.

unresolved_questions: Does task-matched email gold link separated, authored-only passages to the same concrete work-matter Topic within one message?
What is the prevalence of non-contiguous Topic evidence and simultaneous Topic membership under explicit sentence, span, and message denominators?

Does any embedded method correctly combine discontinuity, overlap, shared fragments, and distinct object identities in one task-matched Topic evaluation?
What are A02's discontinuous-only numerical scores, exact multi-fragment decoding rule, and operational uses of Overlapped and OTHER during inference?

Can A03's GPT-4 consolidation revise annotations or recover annotations absent from human candidates, and how is the intended occurrence of repeated text established?
What matching and aggregation rules produced C01's argument scores, and what were the final evaluated event and role inventories?
How much decision-relevant content is absent from the studies' selective gold targets or lost within partially matched spans?
How would any structural transfer perform on contemporary work email with concrete Topic identities? No such result is established by C01's Enron evaluation.

What source-grounded inventory can establish completeness for conditions, exceptions, deadlines, evidence requirements, approval constraints, and decision qualifiers independently of reference summaries?

What are the executed B01 FactCC population and aggregation rules and the executed C01 argument matching rules?
How much do annotation filtering, unresolved role inventories, and conditional gold-trigger evaluation limit C01's account of naturally occurring email ambiguity and omissions?

risk_register.finding: Combining evidence from different semantic tasks could create an unsupported claim of a validated set-valued Topic system.
limitations: The studies do not evaluate a combined system.
Their labels and semantic objects differ from concrete work matters.
risk_register.interpretation_notes: Complementary evidence supports bounded transfer hypotheses. It establishes neither joint capability nor architecture approval.

risk_register.finding: Aggregate or relaxed scores could be mistaken for accurate recovery of the structural cases that motivate G1-A and G2-A.
limitations: A02's discontinuous-only numerical values are unavailable.
No dedicated simultaneous-label accuracy is reported.
C01's argument matching is unresolved.
risk_register.interpretation_notes: Do not infer subgroup performance from a dataset name, aggregate F1, overlap-tolerant scoring, or qualitative success examples.

risk_register.finding: Incomplete decoding descriptions could be silently repaired into capabilities that the sources do not establish.
limitations: A01's relation eligibility and implemented label inventory are incomplete.
A02's subgraph selection and non-Next-Fragment inference roles are unspecified.
risk_register.interpretation_notes: Preserve the described mechanisms and unresolved details together. Missing specifications prove neither an undocumented solution nor necessary model failure.

risk_register.finding: Candidate-assisted annotation, first-occurrence matching, and disagreement filtering could be mistaken for exhaustive and precisely grounded gold construction.
limitations: A03 does not measure candidate coverage or establish mechanically enforced selection.
Repeated source text can remain ambiguously grounded.
C01 removes some disagreement instead of retaining all plausible readings.
risk_register.interpretation_notes: These procedures do not establish complete discovery of memberships, exact provenance, or the prevalence of legitimate overlapping interpretations.

risk_register.finding: Extraction recall, source complementarity, and error-sample percentages could be misread as complete preservation of work-matter content.
limitations: Exact-span errors can reduce argument recall without complete semantic omission.
Reduced document labels and patient-source unions do not enumerate all source content.
Partial credit can conceal incomplete boundaries.
C01's 6% missing-argument share comes from an error-selected sample with an uncertain coding unit.
risk_register.interpretation_notes: No embedded result establishes exhaustive preservation of conditions, exceptions, deadlines, evidence, approval constraints, or decision qualifiers. This boundary does not authorize an engineering experiment.

risk_register.finding: A selective gold denominator can hide decision-bearing omissions.
limitations: The studies do not quantify this risk for msgloom.
C01's disagreement filtering does not reveal how much important content was removed.
risk_register.interpretation_notes: Reference completeness, source completeness, annotation agreement, and model recall must remain separate.

risk_register.finding: Metric names and percentages can be mistaken for semantic preservation rates.
limitations: Metrics use different units, populations, and aggregation procedures.
Several operational definitions remain unresolved.
risk_register.interpretation_notes: B02's statistic named Coverage measures extractiveness over summary words. Kendall correlations, B01 preference scores, FactCC probabilities, and C01 error-sample shares are not decision-bearing preservation rates. Preserve the B01 FactCC and C01 argument-metric and error-distribution exclusions.

risk_register.finding: Gold annotation capability can be mistaken for model capability or corpus prevalence.
limitations: No task-matched Topic output or prevalence evidence is supplied.
C01 shared-trigger prediction evidence is qualitative.
risk_register.interpretation_notes: Human ACUs do not establish automatic ACU extraction. Discontinuous or shared trigger annotations do not establish Topic prediction. Prediction examples do not establish prevalence or a dedicated subgroup accuracy rate.

risk_register.finding: Whole-unit credit and aggregate recall can obscure loss of a critical detail or governing relation.
limitations: This is a transfer risk, not an observed msgloom failure rate.
C01's unresolved matching rules prevent quantifying how often partial credit conceals such loss.
risk_register.interpretation_notes: An isolated timing unit and selected confirmation roles do not validate the full set of decision-bearing categories. The effect of losing qualifier attachment remains unmeasured.

risk_register.finding: Support-task errors can be incorrectly attributed to Topic segmentation.
limitations: The studies do not isolate a Topic segmentation stage or its causal contribution to errors.
C01 includes conditional gold-trigger evaluation and restricted context settings.
risk_register.interpretation_notes: Summarization omissions, event-argument extraction errors, and hypothetical segmentation losses cannot share an inferred rate. Historical evaluated models and Enron data do not establish current work-email performance.

risk_register.finding: Methodological strengthening can be mistaken for gap closure or implementation approval.
limitations: The embedded evidence supports bounded synthesis only.
The exact G3-A empirical measurement remains missing from this evidence set.
risk_register.interpretation_notes: Keep G3-A open. No architecture approval, engineering experiment authorization, or pipeline-state change follows from this synthesis.

risk_register.finding: Promoting C01's domain relevance or publication date into modern business-email Topic validation would misstate the evidence.
limitations: Contemporary communication data and task-matched Topic evaluation are absent.
risk_register.interpretation_notes: Keep direct-email support, corpus recency, and task accuracy separate. Transfer evidence from other tasks also cannot supply email Topic accuracy.

risk_register.finding: Conflating gold representability, qualitative prediction examples, observed prevalence, and evaluation scores could create unsupported claims about overlapping or discontinuous Topic assignment.
limitations: C01 supplies neither Topic labels nor dedicated sharing or discontinuity prevalence and performance measures.
risk_register.interpretation_notes: Each evidence layer answers a separate question. None can substitute for task-matched Topic prediction evidence.

risk_register.finding: Treating argument recall, F1, or the 6% missing-argument category as a content-preservation rate could conceal missing decision qualifiers.
limitations: The gold target is selective.
Matching and some aggregation rules are unresolved.
The 6% category comes from an error-selected analysis with gold triggers and an uncertain coding unit.
